lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: # ruff-29308: [ty] Fix notebook cell lookups after cells with cell magics

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: PR #29308 in astral-sh/ruff, the top layer of a stack: `main` ← #29306 ← #29307 ← #29308. Its base branch `charlie/notebook-position-clamp` is the head branch of #29307, and `sources/pr-29307.json` holds that lower layer. Two bot comments report no ecosystem change and a benchmark gain. No human review comments. A small language-server fix in Rust with a unit test and an e2e test.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Story

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Title: the PR title, or a short name for cell lookups after cell-magic cells.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Why: present, from the PR body. Hover on `x` in a cell after a `%%bash` cell showed the type of `z` from the next cell.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Size: small or medium. Eight files, 155 added lines, two of them snapshots.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Parts: one story, so no parts or one part.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Groups: 1 to 3.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Groups

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 1. Cell index fix: `crates/ruff_notebook/src/notebook.rs`. `cell_range` maps the index among all cells to the index among Python cells, and the new unit test checks it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 2. Server callers: `crates/ty_server/src/document/range.rs`, `crates/ty_server/src/document.rs`, `crates/ty_server/src/server/api/requests/folding_range.rs`, `crates/ty_server/src/server/api/requests/semantic_tokens.rs`. One shared `cell_range` helper replaces the same lookup in two request handlers.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 3. End-to-end test: `crates/ty_server/tests/e2e/notebook.rs` and its two snapshots. One test covers both groups above.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: One group for all eight files, the e2e test inside group 1 or 2, or the `range.rs` helper in group 1 with the code it wraps, is also good.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Must

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `Notebook::cell_range` now converts the cell's index among all notebook cells to its index among valid Python code cells with a binary search on `valid_code_cells`, so a cell after a `%%bash` cell gets its own offsets.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `cell_range` and `cell_content_range` now return `None` for a cell that is not in the Python source, such as a Markdown cell or a cell-magic cell.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - A new `cell_range` helper in `crates/ty_server/src/document/range.rs` replaces the duplicated notebook lookup in `folding_range.rs` and `semantic_tokens.rs`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Folding range and semantic token requests now return no result when `cell_range` is `None`; at base a `None` range gave results for the whole notebook.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - The review names PR #29307, the lower layer of the stack whose head branch is this request's base, as a `pr` source.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - The new e2e test `cells_after_cell_magic` checks hover and semantic tokens on the `x = 1` cell after a `%%bash` cell, and empty tokens for the magic cell.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Good

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Hover reaches the fix through position conversion in `range.rs`, which at base calls `cell_content_range` (added by PR #29307), which calls `cell_range`; so this layer also corrects #29307's clamp for cells after a magic cell.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - The new unit test `cell_range_by_raw_cell_index` uses `valid.ipynb`, where the third cell is the second Python cell and the second cell is Markdown.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - `cell_range` returns the range with the separator newline, and `cell_content_range` returns it without; the PR only adds doc comments to `cell_content_range`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Must not

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not describe the clamp of a position to the end of its cell (`offset.min(cell_range.end())`) as a change of this request; PR #29307 adds it and it is not in this diff.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not describe the notebook module range fix from PR #29306 as part of this request.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not credit the CodSpeed benchmark gain to this diff; the comment compares head with `03ea17f`, not with this request's base.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not put a snapshot in a different group from the `cells_after_cell_magic` test that writes it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not write a group attention that asks for more notebook tests, a cache for `valid_code_cells`, or a new name for `cell_range`; a missing test, a performance idea, and a nit are not attentions.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: - Do not write a group question that asks why `cell_range` now maps the cell index to the index among Python cells; the PR body names the hover bug after a `%%bash` cell that this fixes.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: ## Notes

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The harness hands the producer the base and head SHAs, so this case cannot check that the skill picks the stacked base on its own. The base is the forge's `base.sha` for #29307's head, not the `merge_commit_sha^1` that `pnpm eval:add` writes. The stack was squash-merged onto `main` one layer at a time, so `merge_commit_sha^1` is the squash of #29307 on `main`, and its three-dot diff with this head holds ten files, with files from #29306 and #29307 too. What the case checks is the other half of the rule: the lower layer is a `pr` source, and the review does not describe its code as this change.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The link from hover to `cell_content_range` is `Good`, not `Must`: the reader has to open `range.rs` at base, outside the diff, to see it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Homes: the `cell_range` index fix and the `None` results live in the group summaries. The empty folding and token results for a `None` range fit a `contract` attention on the server group, or its summary. The lower layer #29307 is a `pr` source, and a review that says what #29307 owns does so in prose, not as an attention.
